suite: Sample databases (Chinook, Northwind): equivalent pairs and siblings
metric: Authored pairs on the two schemas under their declared keys, labelled equivalent or different (each 'different' label has a witness database); 8 siblings drop one key, foreign key or NOT NULL the equivalence needs. Provers: structural, algebraic/SMT with the declared constraints and its counterexample search, then the bounded checker for a counterexample.
correctness: 0 wrong: every proof also gives the same result on the real data and no proof is of a pair labelled different; every refutation's counterexample, completed with legal values, satisfies the declared constraints and separates the pair when replayed in DuckDB
held_out: 7/8 proved, 5/5 refuted, 0 wrong (a fifth of the pairs by SHA-1 of their id)
caveats: Authored pairs (54; dev 41, held out 13), not from upstream. Constraint siblings refuted: 8/8. The algebraic prover's executed counterexample search is time-limited, so on a loaded machine a refutation can fall back to unknown (ch-filter-vs-conditional-count was unknown in the first recorded run and is refuted in the latest). No prover was changed for this eval; the first run is the baseline. After merging master the bounded checker was changed to read a declared NUMERIC(p, s) (counterexamples now fit DECIMAL(10,2) columns), and the pairs were rerun: 28/30 refuted, 0 wrong; the rewrites row is unchanged (it does not use the bounded checker).
